basics.name: Abbas Ali
basics.label: PhD Student, Electrical and Computer Engineering
basics.summary: PhD researcher at the intersection of FPGA design and hardware security for cyber-physical systems, developing hardware fingerprinting for physical-layer device authentication that identifies embedded devices from the analog imperfections in their digital switching signals. Validated on production automotive ECUs and extending to drones and robotic platforms. Two years of industry experience in FPGA and RTL design before the PhD.

work.name: University of Michigan-Dearborn
work.summary: NSF-funded research in the Information Systems, Security, and Forensics (ISSF) Laboratory under Prof. Hafiz Malik.
highlights: Hardware fingerprinting for physical-layer authentication of embedded devices
FPGA-based real-time intrusion detection for automotive and IoT systems
Electromagnetic and power side-channel analysis for tamper and counterfeit detection

work.name: IntelliFPGA
work.summary: Design and verification of high-performance digital systems.
highlights: Migrated a legacy Altera codebase to VHDL for Intel Stratix 10 SoC, rebuilding DMA paths, AXI interfaces and IP blocks
Verification in ModelSim and Questa, using ILA to isolate divergence between silicon and simulation
SoC integration across AXI, DMA and the PS/PL boundary into DDR; synthesis and timing closure
